cards.prompt: On our menu, what does "confit" mean?
answer: Cooked slowly, submerged in fat
cards.explanation: Confit means cooked slowly submerged in fat, originally a way of preserving food in south-west France. Our Confit Duck Leg is cooked this way until it comes off the bone, then crisped up to order. Confit garlic is cooked slowly in oil until soft and sweet.
cards.why: Guests often ask, and "cooked slowly in its own fat" sells the dish.

options: The citrus marinade a ceviche is cured in
answer: The citrus marinade a ceviche is cured in
cards.explanation: Leche de tigre (tiger's milk) is the citrus marinade a ceviche is cured in: lime juice, chili, onion and the juices from the fish. In Peru it's also drunk on its own as a shot.
cards.why: Lets you explain the ceviche in plain words.

answer: A garlic mayonnaise
cards.explanation: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise. Ours comes with the Crispy Calamari and Patatas Bravas; the seabream has a saffron aioli.
cards.why: One of the most common words on our menu.

cards.prompt: What's the difference between potato boulangère and gratin dauphinois?
options: Boulangère is baked in stock; dauphinois is baked in cream
Boulangère is mashed; dauphinois is roasted
answer: Boulangère is baked in stock; dauphinois is baked in cream
cards.explanation: Potato boulangère is layered sliced potato and caramelised onion baked in stock, the lighter cousin of gratin dauphinois, which is baked in cream. The name comes from villagers taking the dish to the baker (boulanger) to cook in his oven. It comes with our Lamb Chops.
cards.why: A nice story to tell, and it tells a guest the dish is lighter than they might expect.

options: An Argentinian herb sauce of parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar and oil
answer: An Argentinian herb sauce of parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar and oil
cards.explanation: Chimichurri is an Argentinian herb sauce, usually parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar and oil. Our version has roasted red pepper in it, which makes it sweeter and milder. It's on the Chimichurri Beef Skewers and the Tuna Steak.
cards.why: Helps you describe two of our dishes.

options: A fresh, uncooked salsa of chopped tomato, onion and lime
A sour cream and chive dip
answer: A fresh, uncooked salsa of chopped tomato, onion and lime
cards.explanation: Pico de gallo is a fresh uncooked salsa of chopped tomato, onion and lime (ours also has green capsicum on the nachos). The name translates as "rooster's beak". It's on the M/M Fish Taco, M/M Nacho's and Chicken Avocado Wrap.
cards.why: A word guests see on three dishes.

options: The soft, creamy inside of a burrata: torn mozzarella mixed with cream
A hard aged cheese for grating
answer: The soft, creamy inside of a burrata: torn mozzarella mixed with cream
cards.explanation: Stracciatella is the soft, creamy inside of a burrata: torn mozzarella mixed with cream. It's served with our Tuna Tartare.
cards.why: Guests often know burrata but not stracciatella.

answer: Cured pork cheek
cards.explanation: Guanciale is cured pork cheek, fattier and more delicate than bacon. It's in the Rigatoni Amatriciana, marked (P).
cards.why: A pork ingredient with an Italian name: guests who don't eat pork may not recognise it.

options: A soft, spreadable, spicy salami from Calabria
answer: A soft, spreadable, spicy salami from Calabria
cards.explanation: 'Nduja is a soft, spreadable, spicy salami from Calabria. In our porchetta it melts into the pork as it roasts and carries real heat. The Caliente pizza uses a beef 'nduja.
cards.why: Warns guests about the heat.

options: Italian pork belly, rolled and slow roasted
answer: Italian pork belly, rolled and slow roasted
cards.explanation: Porchetta is Italian pork belly rolled around a seasoned filling and slow roasted so the skin crisps up. It's on the charcuterie platter and is the main of the 'Nduja & Fennel Stuffed Porchetta.
cards.why: Lets you explain a pork dish clearly.

options: A very thin, crisp flatbread from Sardinia
answer: A very thin, crisp flatbread from Sardinia
cards.explanation: Pane carasau is a very thin crisp flatbread from Sardinia, sometimes called "carta da musica" (sheet music) because it's thin enough to read through. It comes with the charcuterie platter.
cards.why: A lovely detail to share at the table.

options: Cured pork neck, marbled and sweeter than Parma ham
answer: Cured pork neck, marbled and sweeter than Parma ham
cards.explanation: Coppa is cured pork neck: marbled, and sweeter than Parma ham. Mortadella is a large, finely ground pork sausage from Bologna. Both are on the charcuterie platter.
cards.why: Helps you describe the platter item by item.

options: Chopped parsley, garlic and lemon zest
answer: Chopped parsley, garlic and lemon zest
cards.explanation: Gremolata is chopped parsley, garlic and lemon zest, added at the end to cut through the richness of the cheese on the Pulled Beef Mac & Cheese.
cards.why: Explains why the dish isn't too heavy.

options: A white sauce of butter, flour and milk
A brown sauce made from stock
An egg yolk and butter sauce
answer: A white sauce of butter, flour and milk
cards.explanation: Béchamel is a white sauce made from butter, flour and milk. Our mac & cheese uses a six-cheese béchamel.
cards.why: A basic sauce that comes up often.

options: A filling made from chocolate, cream and butter
answer: A filling made from chocolate, cream and butter
cards.explanation: Ganache is a classic pastry filling made from chocolate, cream and butter. It's on the Chocolate French Toast.
cards.why: Helps you describe a dessert-style breakfast.

options: A light baked dough used for éclairs and profiteroles
answer: A light baked dough used for éclairs and profiteroles
cards.explanation: Choux pastry is a light baked dough, used for éclairs, Paris-Brest and profiteroles.
cards.why: Guests sharing the Profiteroles may ask.

options: An upside-down tart of caramelised apples on puff pastry
answer: An upside-down tart of caramelised apples on puff pastry
cards.explanation: Tarte Tatin is an upside-down tart of caramelised apples (Royal Gala) with a crispy puff pastry base. Good for sharing.
cards.why: A French classic many guests have heard of but can't describe.

options: A dip of Greek yoghurt, cucumber, garlic and green herbs
answer: A dip of Greek yoghurt, cucumber, garlic and green herbs
cards.explanation: Tzatziki is a dip made from Greek yoghurt, cucumber, garlic and green herbs. It's in the Mediterranean Power Bowl.
cards.why: Vegetarian guests often ask what's in the bowl.

options: Crushed ripe avocado seasoned with lime, tabasco, pepper and salt
answer: Crushed ripe avocado seasoned with lime, tabasco, pepper and salt
cards.explanation: Guacamole is a dip made by crushing ripe avocados and seasoning them with lime juice, tabasco, pepper and salt. It's on the M/M Nacho's.
cards.why: A common question at the table.

options: A soft, slightly salty cheese made from sheep's milk
answer: A soft, slightly salty cheese made from sheep's milk
cards.explanation: Feta is a soft cheese made from sheep's milk, with a slightly salty flavour. It's on the Roasted Beetroot and Feta salad and the Mediterranean Power Bowl.
cards.why: Helps guests choose between our cheese salads.

answer: A fermented soybean paste
cards.explanation: Miso is a fermented soybean paste. In the Crispy Halloumi it makes the mayonnaise savoury and deep rather than sweet.
cards.why: Explains an unfamiliar word on the menu.

cards.prompt: What makes béarnaise different from hollandaise?
options: Béarnaise is made with cream instead of butter
answer: Béarnaise has tarragon and shallots
cards.explanation: Both are egg yolk and butter sauces. Béarnaise adds shallots and tarragon; our hollandaise has cream, vinegar or lemon juice and a dash of cayenne. The Belgian Benedict is the only benedict with béarnaise.
cards.why: Guests choosing a steak sauce or a benedict often ask.

options: A chili sauce of red chili, garlic and vinegar, moderate heat with some sweetness
answer: A chili sauce of red chili, garlic and vinegar, moderate heat with some sweetness
cards.explanation: Sriracha is a chili sauce made from red chili, garlic and vinegar. It brings a moderate heat with some sweetness.
cards.why: Guests who avoid spicy food will want to know.

cards.prompt: What are peas à la française cooked with? Pick all that apply.
answer: White wine
Lettuce
Pearl onion
Pork bacon
cards.explanation: Peas à la française are peas cooked with white wine, lettuce, pearl onion and pork bacon. They come with the 'Nduja & Fennel Stuffed Porchetta (P, A).
cards.why: The side itself contains pork and alcohol.

options: A rich, creamy sauce made from roasted shellfish shells
answer: A rich, creamy sauce made from roasted shellfish shells
cards.explanation: A bisque is a rich creamy sauce made from shellfish shells (shrimp), roasted, simmered and strained. It's why the Cod Fillet carries the (S) mark, and it's the base of the Red Shrimp Linguini sauce.
cards.why: A guest with a shellfish allergy can't have a dish with bisque.
